segments.note: Distributed across then, prefer and avoid without losing the one-journey test, split instruction or any sizing threshold.

activation.note: Covers train creation, modification and review, including relevant wagon-level changes. The exclusions concern edits that do not affect train scope, not exemptions from scope review. Observability notes distinguish mechanically countable size from judgment-dependent coherence and identify the required diff observer. Adding another theme triggers checking, not an assertion that the three-theme signal is already met.

audit.summary: All 22 segments survive at their claimed destinations, including every sizing band and decomposition signal. Application-specific example identifiers remain historical verifier calibration rather than coder-facing requirements; the added rationale and clarifications are declared, and no waivers or shared-node moves are introduced.

segmentChecks.note: The one-journey obligation and split test remain in then; every size band is retained in prefer/avoid and verifier_detail without changing its force.
The one-sentence-without-and test is explicit in then and repeated for evidence and verification.
The 3-7 wagon recommendation and sweet-spot status are intact.
The minimum of two is explicit, including the concrete prohibition on single-wagon trains.
The 8-12 band still triggers review for multiple journeys rather than automatic decomposition.
The 13+ antipattern and decompose instruction are preserved.
The bad 16-wagon multiple-journey example remains in verifier_detail and audit, with a neutralized coder-facing illustration in avoid.
The signals are framed as evidence to investigate for multiple journeys, not as automatic proof.
Multiple AND conjunctions remain a decomposition signal, distinct from the mandatory one-journey test.
Combined setup and teardown of a lifecycle remains an explicit signal.
The exploratory/gesture plus core-mechanic flow mixture is retained in prefer and verifier_detail.
Multiple independent feedback loops remain an explicit signal.
Participants from three or more themes remain an explicit signal.

risks: Coherence and whether a signal actually represents multiple journeys still require judgment, but the coder-facing fields supply the operative test, thresholds, and investigation step rather than an ambiguous implementation requirement.

unobservable: change: needs a new diff-level observer for wagon membership, outcome, flow kinds, feedback loops, and participant themes.
finding: decomposition_signal and journey coherence are LLM-judged; only the wagon-count portion is mechanically countable.

review.summary: The rewrite preserves the sizing thresholds, one-journey test, examples, and all decomposition signals at their claimed destinations. A planner can apply the rule from the coder-facing fields alone; activation is not fully Datalog-deterministic, but the diff-observer and LLM-judged dependencies are explicitly identified. I agree with the auditor's PASS.
